title: Winter warmth did not show a common change in lilac spring slopes in four US samples from 1965 to 2008
abstract: We tested whether warm winters weakened the link between spring warmth and first bloom. We used 9,015 repeated lilac records in four separate US region and period samples from 1965 to 2008. Models included plant and year effects, winter and spring temperature anomalies, and their product. Spring slopes ranged from -2.38 to -3.86 days per C; all four adjusted intervals were below zero. Winter interactions ranged from -0.310 to +0.125 days per C spring per C winter. Only the early western interval excluded zero, and its sign was opposite to the proposed weakening. Three interaction intervals included zero. These results do not show a common winter change in the spring slope. Monthly weather, different lilac types by region, selected long records, missing visit information, and few state clusters limit inference. We do not test a causal climate-change effect, daily chilling, or pollution. The package includes the raw-data recipe, exact source hashes, derived panel, code, all estimates, numerical checks, and a figure.

display.caption: Spring slopes and winter interactions in four samples. Bars give 98.75% marginal intervals. Plant types differ by region. A separate four-test family applies to each term.
